extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners evaluating subject-matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. §101 (Alice/Mayo framework)
extracted.subtask_description: An index of MPEP subject-matter-eligibility examples and the evaluation framework (Step 2A Prong One/Two, Step 2B) used to determine whether claims recite judicial exceptions and whether additional elements supply an inventive concept. Intended to guide claim classification and eligibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Type (Process vs Product)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify each claim as a Process or Product (Composition of Matter, Manufacture, and/or Machine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index identifies whether an example claim is a process or a product (composition/manufacture/machine) to inform which analyses (e.g., MDC for nature-based products) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial Exception Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the claim recites an Abstract Idea, Law of Nature, Product of Nature, multiple exceptions in the same claim, or no recited exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each example is annotated with which judicial exception(s), if any, the claim is found to recite; this classification drives the Step 2A/2B eligibility pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis Mode: Detailed Analysis vs Streamlined Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between a Detailed Analysis and a Streamlined Analysis for evaluating eligibility under MPEP 2106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index indicates whether an example includes a detailed step-by-step discussion or a streamlined (short-form) analysis mapping to Step 2A Prong One/Two and Step 2B outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One: Generally
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2A prong one general inquiry: does the claim 'recite' a judicial exception (abstract idea, law/product of nature) under the general analysis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For post‑June 2020 guidance, the rationale for why a recited concept is an abstract idea should point to one or more abstract idea groupings in MPEP 2106(a)(2). For laws/products of nature, the Step 2A Prong One analysis parallels MPEP 2106.04(II)(A)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong One: Markedly Different Characteristics (MDC) analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform an MDC analysis for nature-based product limitations to determine whether the claim limitation exhibits markedly different characteristics from naturally occurring counterparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MDC analysis is performed when the claim is focused on nature-based product (NBP) limitation(s) (with certain exceptions for process claims). The MDC evaluation considers chemical/physical properties, function/activity, phenotype, structure/form and other meaningful characteristics to decide if the NBP is markedly different.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to Perform MDC Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for whether MDC analysis is required: e.g., when the claim is focused on NBP limitations; process claims generally exempt unless exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claim is focused on NBP limitation(s), perform MDC analysis. If a process claim is not focused on NBP limitations (per MPEP 2106.04(c)(I)(c)), do not perform MDC analysis. If an exception to the general rule applies, MDC should be performed for process claims that are focused on the NBP limitation(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A Prong Two: Exception Integrated Into a Practical Application
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the judicial exception is integrated into a practical application such that the claim amounts to significantly more than the exception itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2A Prong Two asks whether elements of the claim apply, rely on, or use the judicial exception in a manner that imposes a meaningful limit on the exception; examples identify factors (see considerations) that support integration into a practical application. For older examples (pre-June 2020), Prong Two analysis can sometimes be extrapolated from Step 2B (minus WURC consideration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B: Generally (Inventive Concept Inquiry)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Step 2A does not establish eligibility, analyze whether additional claim elements, individually or in combination, supply an 'inventive concept' that makes the claim eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2B examines whether the additional elements are more than well-understood, routine, conventional activity and whether they transform the nature of the claim into patent-eligible subject matter. The index flags when the claim is eligible at Step 2B because it provides an inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvements to Functioning of a Computer or Other Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the claim's additional elements improve the functioning of a computer or other technology as evidence that the claim integrates an exception or provides an inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This consideration supports finding eligibility at Step 2A Prong Two or Step 2B when the claimed elements materially improve technological operation, not merely use generic computer implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular Treatment or Prophylaxis (Prong Two only)
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims in the life sciences/medical space, evaluate whether the claim provides a particular treatment or prophylaxis as a factor for Prong Two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim that applies a natural-law-based concept to a specific, concrete treatment or prophylactic regimen may integrate the exception into a practical application (Prong Two) supporting eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular Machine
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claim is tied to a particular machine (beyond generic computer implementation) as a factor favoring eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recitation of a specific machine or machine improvement that is integral to the claimed invention can support Step 2A Prong Two/Step 2B findings of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular Transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the claim effects a particular transformation of matter as a meaningful limitation supporting eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A meaningful physical transformation of subject matter may show integration of the exception or presence of an inventive concept, consistent with historical machine-or-transformation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Meaningful Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for limitations that add meaningful specificity or technical improvements beyond mere recitation of an exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that include inventive, nonconventional limitations or specific steps that impose meaningful limits on the judicial exception are more likely to be eligible under Prong Two/Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Instructions To Apply An Exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify claim elements that merely instruct practitioners to apply an abstract idea or natural law, which weigh against eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the claim only tells users to apply an abstract idea using conventional steps (mere instructions), it likely fails Prong Two/Step 2B absent other meaningful limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insignificant Extra-Solution Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect additional elements that are conventional or insignificant post-solution activities which do not contribute to eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insignificant additional steps (e.g., data gathering, generic post-solution activity) should not convert an ineligible concept into eligible subject matter under Prong Two/Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of Use and Technological Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the claim's field of use or technological environment meaningfully narrows or integrates the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim tied to a specific technological environment or field of use that imposes concrete limitations may weigh toward integration into a practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well‑Understood, Routine, Conventional (WURC) Activity (Step 2B only)
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2B, determine whether the additional elements are well-understood, routine, and conventional (WURC) activities—which, if true, weigh against finding an inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 2106.07(a)(III) specifies evidentiary options for supporting a WURC conclusion; examples issued prior to June 2020 may not have used those options explicitly and thus may require updated support.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Additional Elements — No Prong Two or Step 2B Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are no additional elements beyond the judicial exception, then Prong Two and Step 2B analyses are not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The index flags examples where claims recite only the exception, meaning no further analysis for integration or inventive concept is possible — such claims remain ineligible absent claim amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract Idea Groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify abstract-idea recitations into groupings: Mathematical Concepts; Mental Process; Certain Methods of Organizing Human Activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical Concepts include mathematical relationships, formulas/equations, and calculations. Mental Process covers concepts performed in the human mind. Certain Methods of Organizing Human Activity include fundamental economic principles/practices, commercial or legal interactions, and managing personal behavior or relationships. Post‑June 2020 analyses should reference these groupings when explaining why a concept is an abstract idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: MDC Characteristics Evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerate specific characteristics examined in MDC analysis: chemical or physical property, function or activity, phenotype, structure or form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performing MDC analysis for nature-based products, examiners evaluate these characteristics (and related properties) to determine whether the claimed product exhibits markedly different characteristics from what occurs in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Pre-June 2020 Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to interpret Examples 1–36 (issued prior to the June 2020 MPEP 2106 revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Examples 1–36, the Step 2A Prong One analysis in the examples may differ from current MPEP 2106 wording; abstract-idea explanations should now point to MPEP 2106(a)(2) groupings. Step 2A Prong Two for those examples can often be extrapolated from the existing Step 2B analysis (minus WURC). The index lists which examples would now be eligible at Step 2A Prong Two and which would require analysis under Prong Two but result unchanged.
